note: GET /api/shell/manifest (BRIDGE.md §5). Three parties parse this shape — the Rust serializer, the Dart updater and the web settings panel — so the field names live here as data rather than in three test files. `bundle_version` is derived from the sorted (path, sha256) listing and nothing else: same bytes, same version, on any replica. It is a 64-character lowercase hex sha256 and parsers must enforce that: it is used verbatim as an on-disk directory name by the shell, so anything else — `..`, a separator, a reserved name — reaches a recursive delete and a rename with the server's word for it.

valid.index_csp: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-Ax9k' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' https: wss:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

verify.name: the hash of known bytes, so both sides agree on the algorithm
verify.note: sha256 is lowercase hex over the exact bytes written, and size is checked first because it catches the common truncation with a message that says so.

invalid.name: an empty file list is nothing to serve
no index.html — a bundle that cannot boot
a path that escapes the bundle directory
a bundle_version that escapes the bundle directory
invalid.note: The id becomes a directory name under the bundle root, and that directory is handed to a recursive delete and a rename when an update installs. A server answering with `../../shared_prefs` — and serving file bytes that match its own hashes, so every other check passes — would have the shell delete the keystore holding the bearer token.

invalid.name: a bundle_version that is not a 64-character hex digest
